findings.title: canManage() grants manage to callers holding only VIEW on all groups
findings.body: In V2 canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because the scope list includes VIEW, a caller who only has the view scope on the all-groups resource is treated as able to manage groups. canManage() is the no-arg check used by requireManage(), so such a caller passes requireManage() in addTopLevelGroup (GroupsResource) and can create top-level groups. Only MANAGE should be accepted in this check.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs and never finds per-group resources
findings.body: The method is documented and consumed as a set of group IDs (used for session GROUPS filter in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource and getUsersCount). Here it adds groupResource.getId(), which is the UUID of the Resource row, not the group ID. Also, per-group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource are never given type 'Groups' (setType is not called), so resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) only returns the all-groups type resource. The callback then passes that resource's ID to hasPermission(groupId, ...), which looks it up by name and does not find it. The net result is that the returned set holds the wrong identifiers, and group-level VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are not reflected in the user search/count filter. The V1 implementation used resource name minus prefix to recover the group ID; V2 needs the group ID, not the resource UUID.

findings.title: NPE when the all-groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: When no group-specific resource is found, the code loads the 'Groups' type resource via getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource returns null if that resource is absent, for example in realms created before the Groups resource type was added to the schema, since there is no upgrade path that creates it. This causes a NullPointerException on any group permission check for a non-admin caller instead of a clean deny. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2 but is new for groups.

findings.title: Per-group canView evaluation replaces the cached global check
findings.body: The previous code computed canView() once and short-circuited the per-group check. The new code filters with groupsEvaluator::canView (i.e. canView(GroupModel)) for every group. In V2 each call re-runs the admin role checks and, when those fail, a full policy evaluation (permission evaluation over the all-groups resource). For large group lists this multiplies evaluation cost by the number of groups. The same regression is introduced in GroupResource.getSubGroups.

findings.title: Javadoc says getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a Stream but it returns a Set
findings.body: The @return tag on getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method signature returns Set<String>. Callers and readers will be misled about the return type and about whether the result is lazily evaluated.

findings.title: No test that a view-only group permission cannot create top-level groups
findings.body: The test suite checks manage-all-groups and per-group permissions, but nothing verifies that a caller holding only VIEW on groups is denied group creation (requireManage()). This is exactly the path affected by the canManage() scope bug, so the regression goes undetected. Similarly, no test checks that group-level VIEW_MEMBERS is reflected in the user list filtering via getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, which is also broken.
